purpose: Teach customer, billing, customer-information-system, and community applications through service, privacy, accessibility, language, records, equity, escalation, and public trust.
staffSummary: Build M60 around one consequential utility situation and one decision: Determine which customer interaction may receive AI support and how the official record, privacy boundary, accessibility need, and human escalation are preserved. The learner must leave with a usable customer and community AI service boundary card, not a collection of definitions.
openingSituation: A chatbot gives a fast billing explanation but cannot see a pending adjustment, language preference, accessibility need, or shutoff protection review.
learnerDecision: Determine which customer interaction may receive AI support and how the official record, privacy boundary, accessibility need, and human escalation are preserved.
analogy: A reception desk can answer common questions, but it must know when to find the person with the full record and authority to resolve the case.
learnerOutcomes: Explain Customer, Billing/CIS & Community Engagement in plain English and connect it to a real water, wastewater, stormwater, or One Water decision.

Distinguish customer record, billing record, public information, personal information, draft response, service decision, accessibility, and escalation without using one term to hide several different jobs.
Analyze the module situation, identify missing evidence, and name the professional consequence of a weak decision.
Compare how the same question changes across drinking water, wastewater, stormwater, administration, engineering, finance, technology, and public leadership.

Evaluate sources, assumptions, limitations, permissions, and human authority using this boundary: Do not automate adverse customer decisions, misrepresent language access, or use personal data beyond approved purpose. Require accessible alternatives and accountable staff review.
Create a usable customer and community AI service boundary card with evidence, roles, limits, review steps, and the next accountable action.
Defend the recommendation to Foundation, Practitioner, and Leader audiences while keeping disagreement and uncertainty visible.
curriculumOutcomes: Give Customer, Billing/CIS & Community Engagement one clear learning job inside AI Across the Water Lifecycle.
Connect the module to a consequential decision and the customer and community AI service boundary card.
Preserve current content, proposals, enhancements, and contributor records by stable identifier.
Separate verified evidence, Hardeep positions, expert interpretation, instructional scenarios, and unresolved questions.
Create an explicit bridge to the preceding and following modules without duplicating their work.
marketingOutcomes: Describe the practical value as helping a learner make and explain this decision: Determine which customer interaction may receive AI support and how the official record, privacy boundary, accessibility need, and human escalation are preserved.
Name the customer and community AI service boundary card as the visible result of the module.
Do not promise savings, compliance, certification, safety, performance, implementation success, or career outcomes without separately approved evidence.
requiredWorkProduct: customer and community AI service boundary card
definitionOfDone: The learner explains the core distinctions, completes the required evidence and decision activities, passes distributed checks, saves a complete customer and community AI service boundary card, and names the next accountable action.
